vesugen.text: Longevity users take Vesugen as a vascular peptide, with the hope that better blood vessel health feeds into a younger overall look. The appearance link is a theory users draw; evidence is cell-culture work and one small Russian human report, with no appearance testing.

crystagen.text: Crystagen is used in peptide-bioregulator circles as an immune and spleen peptide for ageing. Users sometimes fold it into broader anti-ageing stacks, but the appearance link is a loose theory; support consists of small lab reports, with nothing on looks.

chonluten.text: Chonluten is promoted in peptide-bioregulator communities as a lung and airway mucosa peptide. It is used for respiratory health rather than a specific look; evidence is cell-line data, and no appearance use has been studied.

livagen.text: Forum posters pitch Livagen as a peptide that makes cells look and act younger, and treat bioregulators as a non-injectable anti-ageing option. Lab data covers chromatin in old-donor cells; the step to visible ageing is untested in humans.

thymalin.text: Thymalin is a calf-thymus extract used in Russia as an immune drug and promoted for longevity. Looksmaxxing interest is a general anti-ageing hope; the data comes mostly from its developers, with no appearance outcomes measured.

epithalamin.text: Epithalamin, the pineal extract behind Epitalon, is used by longevity enthusiasts hoping to slow ageing, including how old someone looks. Lifespan data exists in flies and rodents; human trials and appearance measures are absent.

cortexin.text: Cortexin is a cattle-brain peptide medicine used mainly in Russia for neurological conditions. It appears in biohacking lists as a nootropic-style option; local trials address neurology, and no appearance use is documented.

retinalamin.text: Retinalamin is an animal-derived retinal peptide used clinically in Russia for glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy. It is discussed in longevity circles for eye health; it has been studied for those retinal conditions, and no cosmetic eye use is documented.

prostatilen.text: Prostatilen is a bovine prostate extract used in post-Soviet urology for prostatitis and prostate enlargement. It appears in bioregulator discussions as a general-health option; data is mostly Russian-language clinical work, with no appearance use.

cortagen.text: Cortagen is a synthetic tetrapeptide modelled on Cortexin and proposed as a brain-tissue regulator in ageing. Interest is in cognition and longevity; it has been studied in cells and animals, with no appearance evidence.

ovagen.text: Ovagen is a Khavinson tripeptide described as acting on the liver and digestive tract. It is mentioned in longevity peptide lists for organ support; published human data is thin, and no appearance use is described.

pancragen.text: Pancragen is a Khavinson tetrapeptide designed to target pancreatic tissue, used in bioregulator circles for metabolic and ageing support. Evidence spans cells, animals and one small human study, with no appearance outcomes.

prostamax.text: Prostamax is a Khavinson tetrapeptide modelled on the prostate extract Prostatilen and used for prostate support. It is discussed in longevity peptide communities; evidence is cell and rat-tissue work, with no appearance use.

testagen.text: Testagen is promoted in research-peptide and longevity communities as supporting testicular function and testosterone, which users link to muscle, leanness and masculine features. The claim is based on developer material, and human evidence is absent.

thymulin.text: Thymulin is a thymus hormone that needs zinc to be active, and appears in peptide and zinc discussions. Human data covers zinc status and thymic function, not supplement use, and no appearance use has been studied.

chain: Tissue repair and hair follicle signalling
thymosin-beta-4.text: Sold as TB-500, thymosin beta-4 is used by lifters for tissue recovery and by hair-loss hobbyists hoping for follicle effects. Human trials cover wounds and eyes; hair data is from mice, and appearance use in people is untested.

thymosin-fraction-5.text: Thymosin fraction 5 is the calf-thymus extract from which thymosin alpha-1 and beta-4 were purified. It matters here as the origin of those peptides rather than as a product people use for looks; no appearance use is documented.

thymopentin.text: Thymopentin is an immune peptide used in some countries for infections and studied in skin conditions such as atopic dermatitis and eczema. Appearance interest is an extension of that skin-disease work; trials on cosmetic outcomes do not exist.

ghrp-3.text: GHRP-3 is one of the numbered growth hormone-releasing peptides, discussed by physique enthusiasts as a way to raise GH for muscle and leanness. It is known mainly from anti-doping lists; human training or appearance trials have not been reported.

ghrp-4.text: GHRP-4 is an obscure member of the GHRP series that physique forums mention alongside better-known secretagogues for GH-driven muscle and fat loss. It appears in anti-doping analytical papers; human trials are absent.

ghrp-5.text: GHRP-5, called the Momany peptide, is grouped with GHRP-1, -2, -4 and -6 as a GH-releasing peptide that bodybuilders consider for muscle and leanness. Evidence is laboratory and anti-doping literature, with no human trials.

livoletide.text: Livoletide is an investigational appetite peptide built for hunger in Prader-Willi syndrome. Fat-loss interest comes from its status as an experimental appetite and body-weight drug; its pivotal trial was terminated, and no cosmetic use has been studied.

lenomorelin-ghrelin.text: Ghrelin is the stomach hormone that raises hunger and stimulates growth hormone, so fat-loss and muscle communities discuss it as a lever on appetite and body composition. It is central to appetite science; use for appearance is untested.

cortistatin-14.text: Cortistatin-14 is a brain neuropeptide related to somatostatin that also binds ghrelin-type receptors, which draws occasional recovery and GH-axis speculation. It has been studied as basic science only, with nothing on appearance.

lum-201.text: LUM-201 is ibutamoren (MK-0677), an oral GH secretagogue that physique users discuss as a pill-form route to higher GH and IGF-1 for muscle and leanness. It is in trials for children with GH deficiency; looks outcomes are untested.

igf-1-des.text: Forum users inject IGF-1 DES locally in hopes of growing the jaw, chin and neck, and stack it with other agents for facial remodelling. Evidence is cell and animal data on protein synthesis; the facial-growth idea is anecdotal.

somatrogon.text: Somatrogon is a weekly prescription growth hormone for children with diagnosed GH deficiency, so it comes up in height discussions. It has been studied in children with deficiency; data for added height without deficiency do not exist.

lonapegsomatropin.text: Lonapegsomatropin is a weekly prescription GH prodrug for children and adults with diagnosed deficiency, and is mentioned in height-focused circles. Trials involve people with GH deficiency; data on height in people without it are absent.

somapacitan.text: Somapacitan is a weekly prescription growth hormone approved for GH deficiency and some short-stature conditions, so height-focused users watch it. Studies cover those diagnosed groups; data on height outside them are absent.

mecasermin.text: Mecasermin is prescription recombinant IGF-1 for children with severe primary IGF-1 deficiency, and it is talked about in height forums as a growth lever. It has been studied in that narrow group; use for height beyond it is untested.
